canal_p02_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_001.text: Tian reached the grain counter before the clerk and found three men leaning on her reading table. They were waiting to buy flour and had mistaken the new meeting notice for a sale announcement. She asked them to move. One said he would gladly move when the canal began paying rent for his impatience. Tian took his empty flour sack, shook its dust onto the table and handed it back. 'Then we can both begin by clearing what we brought,' she said.

canal_p02_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_002.text: Yue arrived carrying the worn gate seal and saw Tian laughing with the flour buyer. Yesterday's argument had made the seamstress seem permanently angry. This morning she bargained for a handful of broken biscuits while refusing to discount her stitching. Yue put the seal beside the household list. Tian asked whether it had a household obligation too. The joke drew Luo's first customer close enough to read the interim notice, and a useful conversation began without anyone announcing that it was important.

canal_p02_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_003.text: Pei Fen needed a chair with its back to the window. Light from the wrong side made the notebook's brown ink vanish beneath her own shadow. Bao moved the table, then moved it back when the new position blocked flour deliveries. They settled on a small stool and a clean white board behind the pages. The retired clerk read three dates aloud without stumbling. Yue had been ready to explain the records before noticing that their keeper could not see them from the seat provided.

canal_p02_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_004.text: By noon, the yard held people from nineteen of the twenty-eight registered households. Four sent written replies; three were away on seasonal work; two had declined the meeting and asked for copies instead. Tian marked actual attendance rather than filling absent chairs with imagined family representatives. A baby slept under the table while its mother spoke. The meeting would have to finish before the afternoon grain boat returned, because that was when half its audience resumed work.

canal_p02_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_005.text: The chair began with a long account of the founding flood. An old boatman interrupted to ask which flood he meant. The chair's date belonged to a smaller overflow five years later. Pei corrected him gently, and he repeated the right year. Han looked embarrassed on behalf of everyone who had trusted the speech. Yue kept the corrected date beside the original note. A practiced public voice could make a wrong opening seem so smooth that the rest of the room forgot to check it.

canal_p02_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_006.text: Tian spoke next, holding a needle rather than a prepared speech. She said her father had completed his work when she was small, then asked why the notice made her complete it again. Han answered that not every household had fulfilled its share. Three people began naming neighbors. Luo struck the bench with the wooden gate seal, startling the baby awake. They would examine individual evidence without turning absence into permission to invent another family's history across a crowded yard.

canal_p02_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_007.text: A widow named no new grievance. She wanted the council to honor her husband's completed work and continue the bank maintenance he had cared about. Tian initially heard that as support for inherited duty. The widow corrected her. She would volunteer a morning to clear reeds while her knee held, but wanted her granddaughter's apprenticeship left alone. The distinction made Tian stop rehearsing her next objection. People could want to keep a practice and still refuse the buyer's version of it.

canal_p02_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_008.text: Han explained the unpaid eighty copper and his mother's first timber delivery. Several listeners remembered the beams, though none remembered the contract's exact words. A man at the back said the old family should forgive the balance because it had profited from the wharf. Han asked whether profitable people lost the right to be repaid. The yard fell quiet. Yue disliked the sale notice, but she could not make that argument better by agreeing with a convenient demand that ignored the actual loan.

canal_p02_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_009.text: Luo drew the private wharf and common bed on a slate. She erased the crane's long swinging arc twice because a child kept touching the chalk. The wharf workers asked about their jobs if Han had to sell the loading gear. Tian said they should choose whether to join a common operating crew. One worker said he preferred his current employer and simply wanted wages paid on time. Tian looked toward Yue, then back at him. 'That preference belongs on the record too,' she said.

canal_p02_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_010.text: The flour buyer produced a receipt for clearing the common drain six years earlier. He believed it released his household forever from all future maintenance. Pei read the receipt and found it acknowledged one paid task, with no broad release. He grew angry because he had carried it carefully through two house moves. Bao said careful keeping could preserve exactly what a paper said without enlarging it. The buyer sat down, still dissatisfied, but allowed the clerk to make an accurate copy.

canal_p02_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_011.text: At the edge of the crowd, a girl practiced the old work song under her breath. Its refrain counted four seasons, then ended with the bank returned to ordinary turns. Pei heard her and asked where she learned it. Her grandmother used it while drying reeds. The song supported Pei's memory of a bounded pledge, but neither woman wanted it treated as the contract itself. Tian asked them to sing it together later. The old words belonged to the bank even if the review could not settle by rhyme.

canal_p02_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_012.text: Bao placed the hollow seal on the table and poured a little clean water through its gap into a bowl. People leaned forward more quickly than they had for the boundary map. He showed how the guide pressed the wood sideways and said the first repair would begin after tomorrow's delivery. The demonstration used ordinary gravity. Han asked whether his workers could help for the posted wage. Bao said yes, if their time was actually free and the shared schedule named the task.

canal_p02_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_013.text: The meeting nearly ended there, until a young father asked whether signing an attendance list made him accept the new work rota. The clerk had put both forms on the same board to save space. Tian separated them, irritated at herself for missing it. The father signed attendance and declined the first paid shift because his wife would be in the grain fields. Nothing in the discussion required him to make the opposite choice. The clean board now held two smaller lists that could be read independently.

canal_p02_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_014.text: Han's oldest wharf worker offered two mornings and demanded that the canal stop describing wharf hands as the enemy. Nobody had used that exact phrase at the meeting, but he had heard it on the towpath. Tian asked who said it, and he refused to turn the afternoon into another accusation. Yue suggested adding the workers' actual contributions to the public repair list. He accepted that, then asked for the wage date as well. Recognition would not buy supper if the payment slipped.

canal_p02_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_015.text: Yue spoke too quickly when someone asked whether the four-season song proved the duty expired. She said it agreed with the original terms, then realized she had not seen those terms. Pei stopped her with two fingers on the notebook. Yue corrected herself in front of the yard: it agreed with Pei's recollection, and the original still had to be found. Han watched without smiling. The mistake gave him a justified reason to question her next confident sentence, and she would have to earn that trust back.

canal_p02_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_016.text: Afterward, Tian said Yue should not have corrected the point so loudly because Han would use it against them. Yue asked whether a quieter correction would make the original appear. Tian turned away, then came back with the baby's dropped cloth. 'I know,' she said. 'I just wanted one person with a cord and a teacher to sound certain on our side.' Yue helped shake the cloth clean. She had wanted the same thing from Elder Yun often enough to recognize the ache beneath the complaint.

canal_p02_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_017.text: The old work song began while the clerk finished copying. Two women knew different third lines. One named willow poles; the other named cedar beams. Pei thought the second version came after repairs introduced a new timber supplier. Han remembered his mother singing the cedar line. The disagreement made the song more useful as history and less useful as a single legal answer. Yue listened to the women's voices find the same final cadence despite everything their middle verses refused to settle.

canal_p02_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_018.text: A shouted warning broke the song. The afternoon grain boat had entered the lower approach early, and its towrope caught under a drying rack on the public path. The boatman pulled harder instead of stopping. A rack leg cracked, tipping wet blankets toward the water. The mother beneath the table snatched her baby up as people rushed outside. Luo called the boatman to release tension. He heard only the crowd until Bao waved the gate seal above his head.

canal_p02_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_019.text: The boat stopped with its bow pressed against the bank and the live rope trapped under broken wood. Nobody had fallen in. A child had scrambled onto a doorstep and stood shaking with one shoe missing. Tian wanted to rescue the blankets first. Luo told everyone to keep hands off the taut line. The rack had obstructed the towpath, but cutting it away under load could send the rope whipping across the very doors they were trying to protect.

canal_p02_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_020.text: Bao placed an ordinary chock against the boat's side from the bank, with a second worker holding it in position. The boatman paid out from his own controlled cleat until the trapped rope sagged. Only then did Bao lift the broken rack leg. Yue moved people behind the doorway rather than joining the live-line work. The child asked for his shoe. She found it in a puddle beside the flour sacks and handed it back, grateful for one small problem that could be solved immediately.

canal_p02_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_021.text: When the rope lay slack, Tian pulled a wet blanket from the reeds and discovered a household receipt sewn into its inner hem. The blanket belonged to the widow who had spoken about her husband's work. She had hidden the paper there during a year when the toll-house roof leaked. Water had reached one corner, blurring the lower amount. Tian stopped wringing the blanket. She laid it flat on a clean board while Yue fetched the clerk, who knew how to dry the paper without rubbing away its remaining ink.

canal_p02_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_022.text: The widow said the receipt had been issued in the pledge's fourth season. Its upper line recorded fourteen days from her household, including replacement turns for a neighbor recovering from fever. The sum remained legible, but the neighboring name did not. Han asked whether fourteen meant her family owed fewer future days. Pei said they must first establish what the original seasonal ceiling counted. The recovered paper added a real work record, not a simple number that could settle every household's obligation alone.

canal_p02_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_023.text: Luo closed the towpath during the rack repair and directed ordinary walkers through the high yard. That route passed two houses whose owners disliked strangers near their grain jars. Tian asked them to permit the short detour and helped move the jars inside. The inconvenience belonged in the plan rather than disappearing because the closure was sensible. A sale map would have called the bank one continuous passage. The actual passage needed doors, neighbors and somewhere to put a child's wet shoe.

canal_p02_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_024.text: Han offered a plank from the private wharf to replace the broken rack leg. The widow refused because she thought accepting it would restore her debt. He looked genuinely bewildered. Bao asked him to write the plank as a one-item gift without any claim on her work. Han did so, awkwardly, on the back of an unused loading slip. She accepted after reading it. A generous act had become difficult because the sale notice had taught people to search every offered object for a hidden handle.

canal_p02_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_025.text: The clerk carried the damp receipt inside and set it beneath a dry cloth weighted at the corners. He would copy only the legible lines until it recovered enough for inspection. Tian wanted to stay beside it all afternoon. Bao needed help moving the broken rack away from the path. Luo needed another pair of eyes checking the towline's contact point before reopening. Yue could do one immediate job while qualified hands handled the others. The meeting's arguments had become a place where ordinary work could begin.

canal_p02_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_026.text: Before anyone chose a task, Pei Fen sat abruptly on the step. Heat and too little lunch had made her dizzy. Yue brought water; Tian brought a bowl of millet; the local clinician checked her pulse and asked her to stop reading small lines for the rest of the day. Pei protested that the receipt might finally answer them. The clinician said the paper could dry while she ate. It was a practical instruction, and for once the retired clerk obeyed a younger voice without debating its authority.

canal_p02_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_027.text: Han remained beside the rack with his wet boot unlaced. His worker pointed out that the accident had delayed their own salt loading too. Han could blame the widow's drying rack or pay for another hauling interval at his private wharf. He chose the latter, after a long look at the grain boat. Yue noticed the choice because nobody praised it. A man defending an excessive claim could still make an ordinary fair decision while the claim remained unresolved.

canal_p02_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_028.text: By midafternoon, the yard had quieted into separate tasks. The baby slept again, Pei ate beneath the awning, the boatman checked his chafed rope and the widow watched her blanket dry. Yue's mistaken statement at the meeting remained in the corrected notes. So did the new receipt, with its damaged corner visible. The next useful hour belonged to preserving evidence, clearing the obstruction or understanding how the towline had caught. She chose where to put her hands.

canal_p02_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_029.text: The damp paper lay beneath its clean cloth while the broken rack leaned against the shed. Bao's crew had the live rope safely slack, and Luo kept the path closed until they understood its contact point. Tian asked Yue to help the clerk preserve the household receipt. Bao asked for ordinary hands moving timber. Luo offered a towline inspection that might prevent the next snag. Each task would change what they could bring to the evening review; Yue could begin with one.

choices.text: Help preserve and compare the household receipt.
Help Bao move and repair the ordinary drying rack.
Inspect the towline's contact path with Luo.

canal_p02_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_030.text: The clerk asked Yue to leave the receipt on its support board. Its wet corner stuck to the blanket seam, and pulling it free could tear the few remaining strokes. Tian cut the thread around the seam instead, giving the paper room without touching its fibers. She had spent years repairing cloth around awkward damage. The archive table now needed that craft more than a confident reader. Yue held the blanket steady while the seamstress worked in tiny, impatiently patient movements.

canal_p02_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_031.text: The widow watched with her hands folded so tightly that her knuckles whitened. Her husband's final work acknowledgment was more than a number to her. She remembered him complaining about muddy boots, then singing the four-season refrain while he scraped them outside. Tian asked whether he had completed neighboring turns as well. The widow said yes, for a sick family. The damaged name might never become legible. They could preserve her attributed account without pretending the paper supplied the missing letters.

canal_p02_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_032.text: Once the seam loosened, the clerk slid a thin dry board beneath the whole receipt. He used no heated lamp, because warmth could change the ink and make the wet corner curl. Yue replaced the outer cloth when it became damp. Tian complained that the procedure resembled watching bread refuse to rise. The clerk said bread eventually supplied lunch. The widow laughed, and the pressure around the table eased enough that everyone stopped leaning over the fragile page.

canal_p02_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_033.text: The legible upper line named the fourth pledge season and fourteen completed days. A small side mark referred to a toll-house book, not a household register. Pei had said the work acknowledgments used that separate book when replacements crossed family lines. Yue wrote the reference exactly and left the unreadable neighbor blank. A specific book request would now reach the archive before the old annex search finished. The damp paper had changed their next action without granting them an instant conclusion.

canal_p02_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_034.text: Tian tried to reconstruct the missing name from the widow's memory. Three families had lived beside her during that year, and two had left after another flood. The clerk asked her to draw all three possibilities on a separate scrap, with no favorite entered on the receipt copy. Yue recognized her own meeting mistake in Tian's first impatient sigh. Certainty would feel kinder to the widow. It might also assign her husband's gift of work to the wrong neighbor.

canal_p02_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_035.text: At the table's edge, the widow noticed the attendance form and asked whether her wet receipt would be kept forever. The clerk explained that its supported original would return after drying, while the numbered copy entered the review. She wanted that in writing because old clerks had once taken papers and lost them. Yue wrote the receiving note, counted the document as one item and let the widow dictate its return address. A small promise became credible through details she could inspect.

canal_p02_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_036.text: The grain buyer returned for his flour and saw the careful drying. He offered an older charcoal copy his mother had made before the receipt was sewn into the blanket. The widow had forgotten asking her to copy it. Yue sent Tian to collect it with the widow's agreement. If it matched, it might preserve the missing reference; if it differed, both versions would stay visible. The buyer seemed pleased that his earlier mistaken broad release claim had not made every later offer unwelcome.

canal_p02_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_037.text: Tian returned with a narrow sheet wrapped around a tea tin. Its copied date matched the receipt, but its completed-days line said twelve rather than fourteen. The reference number was clear. The widow remembered two late replacement days being added after the first copy. The clerk noted that explanation separately and kept both amounts in the packet. The discrepancy complicated their sum while strengthening the case that work records changed over time, something Han's frozen successor list had failed to acknowledge.

canal_p02_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_038.text: By evening, the original had dried enough to lie flat without its seam support. The damaged name remained unreadable. Yue could feel the temptation to call the twelve-day copy the true version because it looked cleaner. Instead she carried both to Pei, who recognized the toll-book reference and requested its surviving companion page. Tian went home with the widow's supported original. Its torn edge would remain part of the family's history, even if the review found a more complete number elsewhere.

canal_p02_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_039.text: At the grain counter, Yue gave Luo the two-copy packet. The keeper added it to the archive request while Bao reported that the rack could be repaired with Han's plank. Nobody's evening summary treated the damaged original as a magical answer. It had revealed a specific fourth-season work entry and a cross-household replacement practice. Those were enough to change tomorrow's search. Yue ate a broken biscuit and discovered she had been too absorbed to notice her own hunger.

canal_p02_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_040.text: The broken rack weighed less than Yue expected, until wet blankets remained draped across its upper rail. Bao stopped her from lifting the whole thing while she was in a twisted stance. They removed the blankets first, then carried the wooden frame from opposite ends along the cleared bank. Tian took the cloth to the widow's door. The task became manageable through changing the load, not asking Yue's two arm pairs to make an awkward ordinary movement safe.

canal_p02_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_041.text: The widow wanted the replacement rack taller so boats' ropes could pass beneath. Bao drew the likely rope height during a loaded tow. A taller rack would still cross the live line if it leaned or if a boat passed at a different water level. The solution needed a location outside the path rather than one favorable measurement. Yue helped the widow move a grain jar inside, clearing a wall position where drying cloth would remain reachable without claiming the whole towpath.

canal_p02_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_042.text: Han's gifted plank was straight but too wide for the old joint. Bao marked the cut while Yue held it on two supports. She had learned enough ordinary craft to keep her hands outside the saw line. A boy asked whether she could split it with sword qi. Bao handed him the broom and said sweeping sawdust would help more. Yue smiled and kept the ordinary board steady. The carpenter's cut produced a fitted piece instead of a demonstration that needed repairing afterward.

canal_p02_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_043.text: At the first fitting, the widow rejected the new position because its afternoon shadow would slow her blankets. Bao looked ready to argue that a safe path mattered more. Yue asked when she usually washed them. The answer was before dawn, not noon. A smaller rack at the side window would catch the morning light without reaching into the rope passage. Bao measured again. The widow was not refusing safety; she was protecting a household task that the first design had made harder.

canal_p02_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_044.text: They discovered that the side window's sill crumbled under the first peg. The timber rack itself was sound, but its attachment would borrow strength from rotten mortar. Bao shifted to a freestanding brace with its feet on paving, keeping the wall free. It used another short offcut from the damaged rack. Yue watched the new frame take shape and understood why a carpenter insisted on seeing the actual house. A beautiful plan could survive on paper while its ordinary support disappeared beneath a thumb.

canal_p02_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_045.text: Han came to inspect the plank's use and found Yue carrying an old rack foot away. He asked whether she thought a written gift was absurdly cautious. She said his notice had made people unsure whether accepting timber meant accepting a duty. He sighed and looked at the fitted brace. The paper had allowed his useful plank to become a simple useful plank again. He did not apologize for the whole auction claim. He asked the widow whether the morning light would reach the new rack.

canal_p02_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_046.text: While Bao tightened the final joint, Yue found the child's missing shoe lace tangled in an offcut. The boy said the shoe had been his older brother's and was too large even before the accident. Tian offered to stitch a tighter heel strap after finishing the sail. Han's worker gave the child a dry pair of socks from the wharf store. None of them attempted to fit that help into the loan balance. The afternoon briefly became a neighborhood again.

canal_p02_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_047.text: The widow tested the rack with a full wet blanket while Bao watched its feet and joints. Yue checked the ordinary walkway clearance at the same time. The frame stayed outside the marked towline corridor. Luo would still set a closure rule for unusual high-water rope heights. A household improvement had solved today's obstruction without claiming that one rack position could answer every future flood. The widow approved the morning-light arrangement and touched Han's plank with a tentative gratitude she chose herself.

canal_p02_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_048.text: Yue carried the broken pieces to the common wood pile only after the widow kept the two she wanted for kindling. Bao recorded the gifted plank separately from paid repair timber so it would not enter the ninety-six-copper work order. The carpenter had not spent its material allowance on this rack. The record mattered, but the room's changed feeling mattered too. Han's worker and Tian now had a small completed task they could mention without opening another argument about who owned whom.

canal_p02_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_049.text: At the grain counter, Bao reported the rack repair and Luo added a towpath-clearance sketch to the review packet. The clerk brought the dried household receipt and its earlier copy from the table. Yue listened to their differences while eating a broken biscuit. She had missed the fragile-paper work, but its results could still be brought into their shared investigation. The new rack held a blanket in morning light. Tomorrow's archive request would follow a fourth-season reference.

canal_p02_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_050.text: Luo gave Yue a long measuring stick and kept the towrope slack on its bank cleat. They followed its former line from the boat to the broken rack, noting the worn polished spots where it had rubbed. One spot belonged to an older turn around a stone post. The newer drying rack pushed the line outward toward the doors. Yue could see the changed geometry without deciding that either a boatman or a household had created the whole problem alone.

canal_p02_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_051.text: The boatman blamed the widow for placing furniture on a working path. Luo asked him why he pulled harder after the first snag. He said an empty boat usually slipped free. This boat carried grain, with a deeper draft and greater resistance. He had used a familiar response under different conditions. Yue wrote the actual cargo state beside the rope path. A rule that worked when a hull was light could become dangerous when its load had changed.

canal_p02_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_052.text: At the stone guide, the rope's outer fibers had frayed on a chipped edge. Han's worker knew about the chip and had wrapped it with cloth last spring. The cloth was gone. Nobody had assigned a replacement check after high water washed it away. Luo marked the guide for an ordinary smooth insert and a dated inspection. She would not blame the widow's rack for a defect that had been waiting beneath every passing rope for months.

canal_p02_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_053.text: Yue asked whether the boatman could use a different bank while the guide was repaired. The opposite path crossed a private vegetable plot. Its owner had allowed emergency passage once but refused a standing towroute across his young beans. Luo accepted the refusal and showed a narrower existing paved turn farther upstream. It would slow boats, but did not require inventing another person's land as a convenient empty space. Yue measured its clearance while geese watched from the bean fence.

canal_p02_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_054.text: The boatman's rope could not reach the temporary turn with its current safe working length. He proposed knotting on a frayed spare. Luo rejected that join under a live loaded tow and arranged another rated ordinary line from the keeper's store. Its use and return would be logged. The boatman would take a slower turn before the guide reopened. Yue felt the consequence in his impatience: a safe alternative had a real cost in time, which the repair plan needed to admit.

canal_p02_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_055.text: Bao checked the stone guide's proposed insert after finishing the rack. The first wood offcut fit tightly while dry but might swell and split its pin under rain. He selected a seasoned piece from the guide's maintenance stock and gave it room to move. Yue had been ready to celebrate the snug fit. Luo told her to remember how the gate itself had begun binding. The canal carried enough wet wood to make tightness a question rather than an automatic virtue.

canal_p02_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_056.text: They used an unloaded rope to test the revised turn, keeping the boat held on its own ordinary lines. Yue watched the path from the bank while the boatman paid out through the guide. The rope cleared the doors and new rack. A later rated loaded trial would be required before normal hauling resumed. The boatman agreed reluctantly because the grain buyer had already complained about delay. Luo recorded the delay as repair waiting, not a second cargo toll.

canal_p02_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_057.text: Han's worker pointed out that the crane closure board could serve the towpath repair too. Tian objected that it belonged to the private wharf. Han authorized its temporary use and asked for it back by tomorrow's loading turn. The loan gave them a visible barrier without requiring a new purchase or claiming the board as common property. Yue carried it to the marked bend. Its red paint looked ordinary and unusually effective against people's instinct to step closer.

canal_p02_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_058.text: At dusk, the path remained closed around the repaired guide while the temporary turn carried one empty boat. The loaded trial would wait for morning light and the keeper's full crew. Yue collected the rope-path sketch, the frayed fiber sample from the boatman's offered loose end and the loan-board return note. Each belonged to a different question. The ordinary accident had given the review another reason to distinguish shared passage, private goods and actual safe working methods.

canal_p02_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_059.text: At the grain counter, Luo laid the path sketch beside Bao's rack report and the clerk's two-copy receipt packet. Yue ate a broken biscuit while the others explained what she had missed. The new fourth-season reference would guide tomorrow's archive request. The guide's loaded trial would precede reopening. Han's board would return on time. The afternoon had produced several small obligations they could actually finish, and one older obligation they were finally learning how to examine.

canal_p02_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_060.text: The clerk's evening summary began with the accident rather than the oldest flood. He recorded the loaded boat, trapped towline, cleared tension and closed repair reach. Then he added the household receipt's two amounts and specific toll-book reference. The meeting's corrected statement about the original annex stayed visible. Yue signed only the work she had witnessed. Han asked for a copy, and the clerk gave it to him. The paper could travel beyond the yard without pretending everybody had seen the same afternoon.

canal_p02_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_061.text: At dawn, the widow's blanket hung on the new rack and caught the first pale light. Tian had stitched the child's heel strap after finishing her sail, making him walk three times before accepting his claim that it fit. He ran toward the grain counter, then remembered the closed towpath and slowed. Yue watched the sequence from the flour-store window. A rule had begun to live in a child's ordinary movement without turning the whole bank into a lecture.

canal_p02_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_062.text: The loaded tow trial used the grain boat's posted working load and the revised temporary turn. Luo kept spectators behind the red board while the boatman eased the line through its ordinary controls. The guide insert held without pinching. Bao checked its movement afterward, before reopening. The boat passed with enough clearance from the doors. The repair had changed a real passage, and its test left a dated record rather than demanding belief in yesterday's excitement.

canal_p02_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_063.text: Han's worker collected the red board before the wharf's loading turn. He asked Yue whether the common repair crew might take more people if the private loading gear was sold. She referred him to the posted paid shifts rather than promising another job. He said he wanted information, not comfort. His current wages were due at week's end. Yue wrote that date in the review's consequence notes. Resolving a public claim could still leave private workers facing a very ordinary frightening Friday.

canal_p02_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_064.text: Tian had offered the worker a stitching partnership during the meeting and now worried she had sounded dismissive of his actual trade. She found him sharpening a loading hook and asked what he preferred. He wanted to keep handling boats, with fewer uncertain paydays. Her answer became a smaller offer: she could mend his lifting gloves at the usual price and tell him when the canal advertised a paid hauling shift. He accepted both. Respect had required changing the plan she imagined for him.

canal_p02_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_065.text: Pei returned with a full breakfast and insisted she was ready to read again. The clinician limited her to the broad notebook, leaving small damaged strokes for somebody with steadier eyes. Pei grumbled about being managed like a granddaughter, then asked Yue to put the clear toll-book reference in front of her. The number belonged to a register stored in the north wharf's old chest. The original public copy had gone missing after a roof leak. Han's private bundle might now contain the surviving companion entry.

canal_p02_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_066.text: Han said the chest also held private loading contracts and would not be carried wholesale into the common room. Tian called that an excuse until the clerk asked which fields they actually needed. The fourth-season work reference could be compared in the wharf office with unrelated pages covered. Han agreed to let An Ru attend when she reached the landing. The archive request narrowed from taking a chest to inspecting a specific recorded transaction, which made a refusal less useful and a legitimate privacy concern easier to honor.

canal_p02_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_067.text: An Ru's reply came with the morning mail boat. She could arrive the following afternoon and spend two scheduled afternoons comparing the surviving records. Her letter asked for the original loan, labor annex, boundary plan and the specific work reference, not every household's personal papers. Pei praised the list until she saw that her remembered blue binding stitch was described as a search clue. Then she laughed. The archivist had somehow corrected her vanity from half a day's journey away.

canal_p02_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_068.text: Yue sent her mother a short account of the canal without describing herself as its rescuer. She wrote about the geese, the room above the flour store and the child whose shoe now fitted. Her mother would want to know whether she had eaten, so Yue added the actual breakfast. Only afterward did she describe the auction notice. The order of the letter surprised her. The canal had begun to feel like people she could picture before it felt like a problem she could explain.

canal_p02_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_069.text: Bao's timber supplier delayed one replacement length because a cart axle broke on the upland road. The first length would arrive tomorrow; the second two days later if the repair held. Bao revised the gate plan instead of asking the crew to wait unpaid at the lock. The ordinary guide work could proceed with the first piece, while the main lower seal waited for the matched pair. The delay would extend leakage. Luo put that real consequence beside the revised schedule.

canal_p02_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_070.text: Han offered a sound cedar length from his shed at the supplier's agreed price. Bao inspected it and found a buried nail where a loading brace had once been fixed. Its clear usable section was too short for the lower gate, though it could serve smaller repairs. He declined the substitution without accusing Han of offering rotten timber. Han seemed disappointed, then asked him to mark the nail location for future buyers. A failed sale could still produce honest useful information about a private object.

canal_p02_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_071.text: The grain buyer wanted the leaking gate opened longer to compensate for yesterday's delay. Luo showed the next cargo turns and refused to erase another boat's appointment. She did offer the buyer the first unused turn if a cancellation came. Tian helped post the revised order at both approaches. Yue remembered the valley's measured water disputes but did not import its schedule here. This canal's boats, leakage and bank uses created their own limits, which had to be counted where they actually occurred.

canal_p02_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_072.text: The child with the whistle came to Bao's bench carrying the cracked mouthpiece. Bao showed him how the split wood interrupted the air, then made a small ordinary repair with wax and a clean reed insert. The boy produced a shrill note that scattered the geese. Luo threatened to assign the instrument a private island if he played beside the gate during boat passage. The boy laughed and ran uphill. Yue enjoyed a morning in which an improved sound created no emergency and required no qi.

canal_p02_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_073.text: Mo Ran loaded his root consignment onto the orchard cart. He had stayed long enough to see the first meeting, but his own delivery could not become a permanent canal duty. Yue helped tie the ordinary cargo rope and checked that he had his papers before the driver left. He told her to ask Han a question that made room for an answer she disliked. It was irritating advice. She accepted it anyway, then watched the cart disappear beyond the willows.

canal_p02_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_074.text: Tian asked Yue why she wanted more paired routes. Yue almost answered with their practical uses, but Tian had watched her ordinary work closely enough to know that was incomplete. 'I want people to stop deciding how small I am before I speak,' she said. Tian considered the answer while knotting a thread. 'You corrected yourself yesterday. I listened more after that, not less.' Yue did not know whether to feel comforted or exposed. She carried the empty breakfast bowl back to Luo's hearth.

canal_p02_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_075.text: Near sunset, Han stood on the private wharf watching a boat approach from upriver. It belonged to his conditional buyer, who had returned sooner than expected. The buyer's agent carried a sealed demand about the loading gear. Han sent his workers home before opening it. Yue saw his shoulders stiffen and remembered the eight-week review date. A legal suspension could protect the canal while accelerating a private creditor's fear. The people inside that fear would still come to tomorrow's gate.

canal_p02_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_076.text: Luo asked the clerk to keep the private deposit agreement out of the household obligation packet until Han chose what could be disclosed for the property review. Its effect on title might be relevant; his unrelated customers' names were not. Tian objected that he had publicly listed everyone else's descendants. Luo said his overreach did not entitle them to repeat it. The exchange ended sharply. Tian took her basket home, leaving Yue to wonder how long a useful alliance could survive without pretending all its members were already fair.

canal_p02_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_077.text: After dark, Bao examined the north platform's support where the crane swung across the common path. The beam had begun shifting under loads heavier than its old working limit. Han's worker had reduced cargo portions, but the buyer's agent wanted a full inventory moved at once. Bao refused to certify the larger lift from a quick look. He asked for a daylight inspection and a clear space beneath the platform. The next property dispute would begin with timber, weight and somebody's urgent claim to private goods.

canal_p02_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p02_078.text: In her room, Yue heard Tian's sewing needle tap against a cup across the lane. The household receipt had led to Han's old chest; the private deposit had brought an agent to the wharf; the shifting crane support needed a real inspection before anything moved. Tomorrow would force those questions together at a place neither wholly public nor wholly private. Yue wrote the three actual tasks on her work sheet, then put her pen down before adding a grander promise.
